title: Does a deception concept vector fire when the model lies but not when it errs?

original_idea.body: Build a deception direction from instructed-lie vs truth pairs; test discrimination across lie / honest-error / honest-correct buckets; deception-vs-honest-error AUROC.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: lie-vs-honest-error discrimination is the make-or-break property of a deception monitor (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Contrastive probe + three-bucket AUROC on one open model; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear success criterion (deception-vs-honest-error AUROC) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fuzzy-reward deception eval, neglected discrimination dimension (level 5).

low_compute.reasoning: Probe + inference, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Deception probes exist; lie-vs-error refinement partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Lie-vs-honest-error discrimination may be partly open.
